entries.content: Shane Kanterman is a Computer Science student at Southern Connecticut State University, expected to complete the program in May 2027, and a current Data Center Technician at InterServer since June 2025. He is also an active member of the university football program. His public portfolio focuses on Linux platforms, server provisioning, networking, deployment tooling, ephemeral CI, and self-hosted infrastructure. He has experience with rack-and-stack work, Linux administration, server deployment, troubleshooting, and practical software delivery. The portfolio lists a Technical Support Fundamentals certificate from Google/Coursera (June 2025).
For professional inquiries, the public portfolio contact section lists Shane's email address: shanekanterman04@gmail.com. That section also provides his public GitHub and LinkedIn links.

The portfolio groups Shane's capabilities into systems and networking, platform and delivery, and software and data. Publicly listed tools include Linux, Proxmox, Nginx, Caddy, Cloudflare, Tailscale, PXE Boot, GitHub Actions, k3s, Actions Runner Controller, Docker, GHCR, atomic releases, Rust, TypeScript, Next.js, Python, PostgreSQL, Git, and Astro. His architecture work emphasizes clear ingress boundaries, isolated workloads, ephemeral CI runners, health checks, atomic releases, and retained rollback paths.

The KanterLabs Homelab Platform turns a small collection of systems into an intentional two-site platform. Its public case study describes hardened edge VMs at both sites, distinct management, ingress, public-origin, and private-origin planes, exact service listeners, split-horizon private DNS, verified edge-to-origin TLS, and default-deny network policy. Public traffic uses dedicated Cloudflare paths, while named Tailscale services provide private entrances without direct workload-network access. Network changes use deterministic configuration, timed rollback, independent management checks, synthetic canaries, and negative exposure tests. GitHub Actions jobs run in disposable pods managed by Actions Runner Controller, with secrets kept outside Git.

Hostlet is a self-hosted deployment control panel for shipping GitHub projects to Docker on a machine Shane owns. It combines a Rust API and local deployment agent with a Next.js dashboard, PostgreSQL, Docker, Caddy, Cloudflare, and GitHub OAuth. The v0.1.0 local-machine beta includes deployment logs, health checks, rollback, encrypted app settings, public URL controls, and release packaging. The scope is deliberately local-only so reliability, cleanup, and security boundaries could be handled before remote agents.

Sandbox Factory is Shane's private-preview platform for requesting short-lived development workstations without exposing hypervisor credentials to the browser. An Access-protected static dashboard calls fixed same-origin workflows; a Go broker verifies identity, enforces quotas and idempotency, stores durable lifecycle state in PostgreSQL, and owns the scoped Proxmox path. New requests use one of four fixed Debian resource presets. The design includes adaptive sanitized telemetry, an isolated guest network with a forwarding-only SSH jump path, lease expiry, serialized lifecycle work, and deletion that remains visible until the broker verifies the guest and managed storage are absent. The checked-in default is report-only, so live mutation remains gated behind explicit infrastructure acceptance checks.

The Dual-Origin Portfolio Deployment case study describes a static Astro portfolio delivered as the same immutable release to OVH and homelab Nginx origins. Cloudflare provides public TLS, health checks, and production load balancing. GitHub Actions deploys beta artifacts directly over private management paths to both isolated candidate lanes, verifies each candidate locally, then promotes the exact artifact to both production origins with coordinated rollback. The design separates public ingress, private deployment, and workload responsibilities while retaining commit-addressed releases for recovery.

Shane's InterServer Data Center Technician experience covers rack-and-stack, cabling, Linux, Windows and Proxmox installation, PXE-based imaging, inventory checks, hardware diagnostics, failed-drive and memory troubleshooting, NIC and boot troubleshooting, and deployment documentation. The case study emphasizes evidence-based diagnosis, deliberate sequencing, communication, and operational care around live infrastructure.
